-#      Binds a filled column data collection to the statement under a name.
-#      Makes the collection visible to the statement as a table named name, by
-#      injecting a common table expression into the parsed statement. The
-#      statement can then be bound, prepared, or executed through the existing
-#      surface; each execution scans the collection's contents at that moment.
-#      Supported statement types are SELECT, INSERT, UPDATE, DELETE, and MERGE
-#      INTO; any other type is rejected with ERROR_INPUT_INVALID.
-#      name is a borrowed string view and must be non-empty. A name already
-#      present in the statement's CTE map (from the SQL text or a prior call) is
-#      rejected with ERROR_INPUT_INVALID. The binding shadows any catalog table
-#      named name, following standard CTE semantics.
-#      By default the collection's columns bind as col1..colN. Pass column_names
-#      to bind them under caller-chosen names instead, so the statement can
-#      reference them directly (FROM buf) without an alias. When supplied,
-#      column_count must equal the collection's column count; a mismatch is
-#      rejected with ERROR_INPUT_INVALID. Pass (NULL, 0) for the col1..colN
-#      The collection is borrowed: the caller keeps ownership and must keep it
-#      alive while the statement, any prepared statement created from it, and any
-#      result executed from it are live, and must not reset or destroy it while
-#      such a result is live, because result scans reference the collection's
-#      buffers. An empty collection is a valid binding. Multiple collections

+ * Binds a column data collection to the statement under a name.
+ * Makes the collection visible to the statement as a table named `name`, by adding a common table expression to the
+ * parsed statement. The statement can then be bound, prepared or executed as usual; each execution reads the
+ * collection's contents at that moment, so a prepared statement can be executed again after the collection was cleared
+ * and refilled. Supported statement types are SELECT, INSERT, UPDATE, DELETE and MERGE INTO; any other type is rejected
+ * A name the statement already defines as a common table expression, in its SQL text or by a prior call, is rejected
+ * with `ERROR_INPUT_INVALID`. The binding shadows any catalog table named `name`, as a common table expression does.
+ * By default the collection's columns are named col1..colN. Pass `column_names` to name them instead; when supplied,
+ * `column_count` must equal the collection's column count. Pass NULL and 0 for the default names.
+ * The collection is borrowed: the caller keeps ownership and must keep it alive, and must not clear, reset or destroy
+ * it, for as long as the statement, any statement copied or prepared from it, or any result executing it is live. An
+ * empty collection is a valid binding. Several collections can be bound under distinct names.

+ * @param column_count The number of names in `column_names`. 0 for the default names; otherwise the collection's column

+TEST_CASE("V2 statement collection: INSERT and SELECT over a bound collection", "[capi_v2][statement_collection]") {
+	REQUIRE(RunSql(fx.conn, "CREATE TABLE t (v BIGINT, tag VARCHAR DEFAULT 'seen')") == DUCKDB_V2_ERROR_NONE);
+	// The columns are named col1..colN by default.
+	auto insert = CollParse(fx.conn, "INSERT INTO t (v) SELECT col1 FROM buf");
+	REQUIRE(CollQuery(fx.conn, "SELECT v FROM t ORDER BY v") == std::vector<int64_t> {1, 2, 3});
+	REQUIRE(CollQuery(fx.conn, "SELECT count(*)::BIGINT FROM t WHERE tag = 'seen'") == std::vector<int64_t> {3});
+	// Or as the caller names them, and several collections bind under distinct names.
+	auto join = CollParse(fx.conn, "SELECT a.x FROM a JOIN b ON a.x = b.y ORDER BY a.x");
+	// The collection drives UPDATE, DELETE and MERGE INTO too.
+	auto del = CollParse(fx.conn, "DELETE FROM t WHERE v IN (SELECT col1 FROM gone)");
+	auto update = CollParse(fx.conn, "UPDATE t SET tag = 'updated' FROM upd WHERE t.v = upd.col1");
